Mick Jagger has won a two-year battle to stop a 29-storey high-rise from being built next to Battersea Bridge on the River Thames in London.

The 82-year-old was joined by other celebrities including Felicity Kendal, Eric Clapton and comedian Harry Hill in the fight to oppose the 100m development from going ahead.

Proposals to build the block of 110 luxury flats were dismissed by Wandsworth Council and the Greater London Authority last year but developers Rockwell Property appealed the decision.

A planning inspector rejected the appeal on Thursday, saying that the project would be detrimental to both the appearance and heritage of the local area.

“I have lived in this area for a long time and I care about what happens to it,” the Rolling Stones musician told the Chelsea Citizen in March earlier this year.

“If this goes ahead, it could lead to more tall buildings being built … changing this wonderful stretch of the Thames riverside forever.”

Meanwhile, Mr Clapton said that the building would create a “free-for-all for other developers to build towers along the river”.

open image in gallery Jagger had previously said that the development would change the riverside ‘forever’ ( Getty )

“These developers don’t give a damn what anyone thinks,” he said. “They are just in it for the money.”

Joanna Gilbert, an inspector appointed by the secretary of state said: “The proposal would cause harm to townscape character in several identified views from different directions and differing distances... This would have an adverse effect on the character and appearance of the area.”

She added: “[It] would be taller and bulkier than other existing buildings, rendering it highly noticeable. The proposal would cause a dramatic change to the skyline in views along this part of the [Thames] embankment. Overall, this change would be detrimental.”

open image in gallery The building plans have been dismissed ( Rockwell )

“The proposal is not exemplary, extraordinary, remarkable or distinctive, just tall. It would not adorn the London skyline and would not form part of a ribbon cluster of tall buildings, but would appear alien and isolated in its very height in this location, harming spatial character.”

Rockwell said in a statement, according to The Times: “We are obviously disappointed with the decision as we firmly believe in this regeneration project. We wanted to see it delivered and made a number of changes to the scheme following feedback from the public.”

“We did not compromise on quality, using the world-renowned architects, Farrells, so it is disappointing the inspector did not share our view that this would be a great addition to London’s skyline.”

This New York grande dame is back and better than ever after a scrupulous eight-year transformation, complete with a marble-columned cocktail bar, a buzzy contemporary restaurant, and sophisticated rooms

Location

Occupying a full block between Park Avenue and Lexington, a stay at the landmark Waldorf Astoria New York brings you to the heart of Midtown East. This thrumming business and shopping hub is close to various well-known NYC landmarks, like the Chrysler Building, Grand Central Station and the United Nations Headquarters. It’s also a hop from all the luxury boutiques and flagship shops lining Fifth and Madison Avenues. For culture, Museum Mile on the Upper East Side is a pleasant 20-minute stroll away through Central Park or short taxi ride. Here you’ll find the Met, the Frick and the Guggenheim.

From JFK airport, either take the AirTrain to Jamaica Station, then the E subway train to Lexington Ave/53rd St; the LIRR to the Grand Central Terminal (less than a 10-minute walk from the hotel) or a taxi.



The vibe

open image in gallery Peacock Alley is home to a Steinway piano that once belonged to Cole Porter ( Hilton )

Born from a 19th-century family rivalry on Fifth Avenue, the Waldorf Astoria started life as two separate hotels built side-by-side that defined opulent Gilded Age hospitality. It relocated to its current iconic Park Avenue location in 1931 and its recent eight-year transformation celebrates its Art Deco heyday.

The history is palpable from the moment you whirl through its storied revolving brass doors and sashay up one of several marble staircases into Peacock Alley, its signature bar and lobby lounge which is the social heart of the hotel. It’s home a Steinway piano that once belonged to the American composer Cole Porter and is home to the hotel’s most iconic feature, the Waldorf Astoria Clock, made for the 1893 Chicago World’s Fair.

Service

The Waldorf Astoria New York has a huge team of welcoming and efficient staff. Whichever entrance you choose to make – Park, 50th or the private historic 49th porte-cochère – friendly, uniformed staff await your arrival, ready to whisk away your luggage and usher you inside.

As I wandered into the Library Lounge, a suited staff member manning a drinks trolley offered me a glass of champagne to sip while checking in, before I was escorted all the way to my room by another.

Despite the hotel’s landmark status and excellent reputation, service here isn’t over the top or overly gushing as you might expect. Everyone I encountered seemed to have gracefully mastered the art of understated attentiveness.

Bed and bath

There are 375 rooms and suites – whittled down from its original 1,400 to create fewer, larger rooms (starting at 570 square feet). Plush king-size beds, work desks and seating areas feature in most.

City views vary depending on what side of the hotel you’re on, with some facing out over Lexington Avenue and others Park, but both guarantee to offer impressive people watching.

open image in gallery A Junior Suite with a plush king-size bed ( Hilton )

The classic, cream-toned decor reflects the hotel’s air of timeless sophistication, with elegant furnishings and plush fabrics, as well as statement ceramic lamps and abstract artworks, which add a contemporary feel.

Spa-like marble bathrooms are kitted out with Aesop products and have deep tubs, rainfall showers, single or double marble sinks and separate Japanese Toto toilets with heated seats. Suites have an adjacent dressing room area with a vanity table.



Food and drink

There are two restaurants and a bar at the Waldorf Astoria New York. All-day Lex Yard Brasserie has contemporary fine dining covered. It’s set within two dramatic spaces across different floors, each with a distinct atmosphere. Both have contemporary decor inspired by the jazz age – the dazzling downstairs space feels more buzzy; while upstairs, where breakfast is served, is more plush and peaceful.

Chef Michael Anthony’s pared-back menu features beautifully presented crowd-pleasing dishes, including crispy baby artichokes, roasted and fried chicken – and the Waldorf Salad (a crunchy, creamy mix of apple, celery, walnuts and grapes dressed in mayonnaise, invented at the hotel.)

The daily breakfast served a la carte was a highlight of my stay. Not only for the light and fluffy baked egg frittata stuffed with goat's cheese and cherry tomatoes, but also for getting to sit in one of the beautiful light-green banquettes.

Vegetarian, vegan and gluten-free options are available.

open image in gallery Lex Yard Brasserie has a pared back menu, including the Waldorf Salad ( Hilton )

Hiding in the Park Avenue lobby, which features the famous Wheel of Life mosaic from 1939, is Japanese restaurant Yoshoku. It serves elegant tasting menus for dinner which can be paired with sake, as well as offering a Japanese afternoon tea.

For drinks, Peacock Alley is a glorious, storied highlight not to be missed. It serves a classic cocktail list inspired by the hotel’s history. Think a smooth Waldorf Martini, or seasonal signatures such as the Lottery Pick, a smoky mix of mezcal, lime, pineapple, passion fruit, agave and ginger beer.

Facilities

open image in gallery The Guerlain spa has 16 treatment rooms ( Guerlain )

The 24-hour fifth-floor gym is generously kitted out with high-tech LifeFitness equipment including running machines, cross-trainers, exercise bikes, as well as free weights. Indulging in a treatment at the plush Guerlain Wellness Spa is an absolute must, with its 16 treatment rooms (including two couples’ suites.) The Harmony Jet Lag massage is a decadent hour-and-a-half treatment carried out to the sound of Tibetan singing bowls, which are said to soothe the nervous system and induce a good night’s sleep.

Save time to enjoy the experiential post-treatment relaxation areas, plus the sauna, steam room and arctic cave (for cold therapy).



Accessibility

The hotel has 32 adapted rooms with wide bathroom doors, roll-in showers and grab bars.

Pet policy

Dogs are welcome to stay free of charge at the Waldorf Astoria New York and dog-friendly treats are available on request, such as welcome bottles of “CharDOGnay” or “ZinfanTAIL”. The hotel also offers gourmet food, plush beds, water and food bowls.

Check-in/check-out

Check-in is 4pm; check-out is 12pm.

Family-friendly?

The Waldorf Astoria New York’s newly-renovated spacious junior suites are perfect for small families, while larger ones which can easily be accommodated in interconnecting rooms. There’s no babysitter service or kids’ club currently.

open image in gallery The ‘Premier’ one bedroom suite with a Park Avenue view ( Hilton )

At a glance

Best thing: How it feels to enter this majestic world through its revolving doors and be part of a new generation who get to sleep and eat within its storied surroundings.

Perfect for: Celebrating a special occasion; a romantic trip; a girl’s getaway; business trip; or a family holiday for those with older children.

Not right for: A low-key break where the main aim is rest and relaxation.

Instagram for: The iconic Peacock Alley bar, while sipping a Waldorf Martini as the jazz band plays.

Ellie was a guest of the Waldorf Astoria

Phone: +1 212 355 3000

News.content:
Step

Pick the chicken pieces out of the marinade and put them on a baking tray with a rim, or in a roasting tin (discard the marinade). The chicken needs to lie in a single layer, skin-side up, but there shouldn’t be a lot of room around each piece, otherwise the juices will run off and burn. Sprinkle a little salt over each piece.

News.title: Soy-sesame-honey chicken
News.content:
Step

Put 7 tbsp soy sauce, 2½ tbsp honey, 3 tsp sesame oil, the juice of ½ lime, 4 grated garlic cloves, 4cm cube fresh ginger (peeled and grated) and 1½ tsp chilli flakes (or you can use a chilli sauce, to taste, if you like), into a dish in which the chicken will fit. News.title: Speedy creamy fettuccine with lemon
News.content: This is simple but luxurious (it’s rich so you don’t need a huge serving). Add cooked broccoli, shreds of parma ham, lardons (tossing them in at the last minute), or just have it as it is.

News.content:
Step

Cook for another couple of minutes, stirring, then taste – it should be quite sour, with an underlying sweetness from the onions and the flavour of fenugreek. It will be quite strong, but you’ll be eating with the fish flesh, remember. Adjust the seasoning if you need to.

News.title: Top WHO official: I’m relieved it isn’t bird flu, but we’re in a ‘make or break’ phase for hantavirus
News.content:
When Maria Van Kerkhove first heard about a lethal and unexplained outbreak on a polar cruise, her mind jumped to bird flu – and her heart sank. Was this the beginning of the H5N1 pandemic that scientists have long predicted?

The signals were alarming. The index cases had been bird watching in Argentina, where avian influenza has been detected in farmed poultry and wildlife, and the ship had made further stops in a series of remote and ecologically diverse ports. Worse, there was already a cluster of three cases. If it was bird flu it had almost certainly started to spread between people.

There was relief when the results came back negative. A specialist lab in South Africa confirmed the patients had not been stricken with bird flu, nor legionnaires disease. The pathogen was Andes hantavirus.

For Dr Van Kerkhove, the director of the Department of Epidemic and Pandemic Preparedness and Prevention at the World Health Organization (WHO), the results felt like a bullet dodged.

“It’s strange but yes, I was relieved that it wasn’t a zoonotic influenza, because of the link with the first three cases,” she told the Telegraph from her office in Geneva.

“If it had turned out to be a zoonotic influenza, and we already knew there were three cases epidemiologically linked … that would have been a bit more concerning.”

News.title: Roast chicken thighs with tomatoes, fennel seeds, chilli and honey
News.content: A bung-in-the-oven dish. I love fennel, honey and chilli together – they taste so summery. To have something to eat on the side, just quarter or halve baby potatoes, toss them in a roasting tin with 1 ½ tbsp of olive oil, seasoning and the leaves from two sprigs of rosemary, and roast on another shelf at the same time as the chicken. All you need in addition is a green salad. Sprinkling sea-salt flakes on to the chicken ensures a crispy skin.

News.title: Asparagus, peas, radishes and burrata salad with anchovy-pistachio dressing
News.content: You can call this a salad or a ‘platter’ or whatever you like. It’s good for lunch (serve with good bread or little boiled Jersey Royal potatoes) as well as a starter. Burrata is expensive and not everyone loves the creaminess so it’s fine to use mozzarella instead (slice or tear it and drizzle it with some extra virgin olive oil). The anchovy-pistachio relish is also great with roast lamb, griddled chicken and meaty fish, such as tuna. You can replace half the pistachios with almonds or pine nuts.

Sports.title: Chelsea have horror record against Man City but FA Cup final would be fitting time to break Wembley jinx
Sports.content:
TWO heavyweights going head-to-head in an FA Cup final.

But ironically, both Manchester City and Chelsea head to Wembley hoping to end their losing runs.





City became the first team in the history of the world’s oldest competition to reach four successive finals with the semi-final comeback 2-1 win over Southampton.

But after beating rivals United in 2023, they lost in a repeat 12 months later before Crystal Palace claimed their maiden major trophy a year ago.

Now they are just 90 minutes away from joining opponents Chelsea as the only team to lose three FA Cup finals in a row.

The Blues’ horror run preceded the City final dominance.



Arsenal beat them in 2020, Youri Tielemans’ wondergoal sealed the 2021 final for Leicester and Liverpool snatched it on penalties after a 0-0 draw in 2022.

Ironically, that Liverpool result was a carbon copy of the League Cup final three months earlier.

And it all feeds into a pretty wretched domestic finals record for Chelsea in recent times.

As well as their three FA Cup defeats, the West Londoners have also lost their last three League Cup finals – to City on penalties in 2019, the aforementioned Liverpool one in 2022 and then again to the Reds in 2024.



However, they fare much better in international finals – winning the Europa League in 2019, the Champions League in 2021 and then both the Conference League and Club World Cup in 2025.

And the Champions League result is a significant one.

Chelsea won the 2021 Champions League final, beating Saturday’s opponents City in Porto thanks to Kai Havertz’s penalty.



Since that match, though, City are unbeaten in all 13 matches against the Blues, winning ten and drawing three.

Pep Guardiola will want his star man to pack his shooting boots for a trip to the national stadium.

That is because Erling Haaland has never scored at Wembley.

In fact, it is the only stadium he has played in at least twice and not scored.

Haaland’s record is eight matches, 601 minutes, 11 shots… and zero goals.



And despite lifting seven trophies with the Etihad club – and closing in on a third Premier League golden boot – the Norwegian goal machine is yet to score for City in a final.

He has racked up 15 shots across nine finals, including the Community Shield.

It means his last final goal came way back in May 2021 when his double helped Borussia Dortmund beat RB Leipzig in the DFB Pokal showpiece.

Like Haaland, Chelsea are pretty goal shy under the arch, too.



Their last eight Wembley matches have yielded just seven goals in total – four for, three against.

Interestingly, City and Chelsea arrive at the home of football with identical records in the FA Cup this season.

Chelsea beat Championship trio Charlton (5-1), Hull (4-0) and Wrexham (4-2) before thrashing League One Port Vale 7-0 in the quarters.

They then saw off Leeds 1-0 thanks to an Enzo Fernandez header in the semi as Calum McFarlane took over from Liam Rosenior.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

City, meanwhile, crushed League One Exeter (10-1), League Two Salford (2-0) then Premier League duo Newcastle (3-1) and Liverpool (4-0) to set up the semi against Championship promotion-chasing Saints.



It means both sides have an aggregate score of 21-3 – but something will have to give on Saturday afternoon.

Sports.title: Secrets of England’s World Cup hideout… pimped-up basketball court, oxygen pods & Tuchel’s cheeky ‘promise’ if team WINS
Sports.content:
DEEP in Mid-West fly-over country, Kansas City was long regarded as a sleepy, footballing backwater.

The old cowtown is more famous on the global sporting stage for its Superbowl-winning gridiron team and their superfan Taylor Swift.



Now the city that glories in being labelled the Heart of America has used its folksy charm to woo England’s superstar squad who will based here for the World Cup.



Local organiser Alan Dietrich told me Three Lions coach Thomas Tuchel secured the booking over a game of padel tennis and a decent feed at “luxury” Kansas seafood restaurant Eddie V’s.

Genial Alan – in charge of base camps in Kansas City – revealed: “We played padel. Coach (Tuchel) is very good and very competitive. It wasn’t a casual game, you could just tell his intensity.

“Jake Reid – CEO of (local football team) Sporting KC – and myself then went out to dinner with coach and his staff and we really bonded.

“That’s when coach said, ‘When we win (the World Cup), we all get a tattoo. As partners are you in?’

“We looked at each other, then said, ‘Yes, we’re in.’ The design will be the trophy with England elements added to it.’”



Currently tattooless, 64-year-old Alan gestured to his upper arm and told me: “I’ll have it there, I think it will age well.”

Yet, the Three Lions aren’t the only ones who will follow the yellow brick road for the delights of KC, as locals call this sprawling city that straddles the Kansas/Missouri state line.

Also establishing their HQs in this understated prairie town of 2.2million are Lionel Messi’s reigning champions Argentina and Virgil van Dijk’s Holland. Algeria have also chosen to base themselves here.

Local police chief Eric McCullough said: “It’s like having six Super Bowls.”



It would make a decent World Cup Group of Death and unleashed what sports newspaper the Athletic called “the heavyweight battle for World Cup base camps”.

And, 40 years on from Diego Maradona’s Hand of God, England’s arch rivals Argentina have won the race to secure what many regard as the city’s premier training facility.

Donning my 1966 red Three Lions strip, I took a tour of the South American’s base, the Compass Minerals National Performance Center.

Sitting in the changing room where Messi will shortly hold court, I surveyed a training complex fit for the Greatest of All Time.



The facilities – used by MLS team Sporting Kansas and the US men’s team – include a smoothie bar, boot driers and a Zen Room where the Little Master can relax and meditate.

It also boasts a 12,870 square foot gym, large hot and cold plunge pools and hyperbaric oxygen chambers to aid muscle recovery.

Outside there are five state-of-the-art football pitches fit to grace the world champions.

So how come Argentina got the plush pick of the training bases?

Under FIFA rules, the South Americans and Holland got first dibs because they have fixtures in KC itself. England – who play their group games in Dallas, Boston and New Jersey – had to wait.



Eventually, they secured Swope Soccer Village 20 miles across the city from Argentina’s camp.

Dwarfed by Argentina’s base, as we toured the site Alan describes the changing areas and team talk suite as “intimate”.

England will erect a giant air-conditioned marquee on one of the pitches at the complex used by Sporting KC’s reserves and their academy players.

In the past Manchester United, Manchester City, Newcastle United and Stoke City have all used the £15million facilites.

Fringed by thick woodland and bathed in 30C sun, the tranquil setting lends the training camp a laid-back feel.



And playing a few passes on the neatly-cropped turf on one of England’s three training pitches, I can attest to it being as true as snooker table baize.

Alan insists Tuchel actually prefers Swope to Argentina’s high tec complex: “It’s a more compact facility but what he likes about that is it keeps everybody together.

“So he’s building this team and building their camaraderie and closeness to each other.”



So why has the cream of international football beaten a path to America’s 38th-largest city tucked away on the plains of Middle America?

Nicknamed the Barbecue Capital of the World, KC was long regarded as a footballing backwater.

Back in the 1980s local university coach Tony Tocco called it a “hick town” for football.

Kansas City Wizards, the predecessors of Sporting KC, are described on the club’s own website as having had a fanbase with the reputation of “screaming 12-year-olds with plastic noisemakers in an empty, chasmal Arrowhead Stadium”.

Yet, in the last 15 years it has invested some £480million into top tier training facilities to earn another of the city’s varied nicknames, the Soccer Capital of America.



It will host six World Cup matches including a potential blockbuster quarter final when Messi could face Cristiano Ronaldo. (It would require Argentina and Portugal to top their respective groups).

The games will played at the Arrowhead Stadium, home to leading American football team the Kansas City Chiefs

Chiefs’ tight end Travis Kelce is rumoured to be marrying fiancee Taylor Swift this summer at an as yet undisclosed location.

The pair – who share a 17,000-sq ft gate mansion located in the affluent Leawood suburb when in town – have been spotted at restaurants and bars around KC.

Gift shops hawk merch dedicated to the pair including tee shirts proclaiming: “Here for the drinks and Travis Kelce’s butt”.



Alan says Tuchel plumped for KC because “he loves the location – in the centre of the US.

“And he loved the ability to get around the city and they’re staying at the Inn at Meadowbrook and it’s a beautiful place.

“So he felt like that would be a perfect environment for the players.”



Taking an Uber ride to England’s boutique hotel in upmarket Prairie Village – ten miles from Swope – I have to cross the state line from Missouri to Kansas.

It means a whole new set of laws. Recreational marijuana is legal in Missouri but not in Kansas.

While in Missouri you can buy hard liquor in a grocery or convenience store but not on the other side of the state border.

The taxi passes through Truman Show-esque leafy suburbia dotted with white clapboard homes with double garages.

Locals fly the Stars and Stripes from neatly-manicured lawns in what is the very picture of wholesome Middle America.



In a different time zone to the fleshpots of New York and Los Angeles, it feels like another country.

I ask the driver if he’s heard of Harry Kane and he shakes his head. Other locals tell me the players will be able to move around the city without being mobbed.

Set in rolling park land, the Inn by Meadowbrook was recently described in one recent Tripadvisor review as “the Jewel in the Kansas City crown”.



Enjoying a Japanese lager on the sun-dappled hotel terrace, I listened as the sound of gushing fountains in the three adjoining lakes mingled with the clink of glasses and laughter of well-healed guests.

Keen angler Phil Foden may like to know the lakes are stocked with bass and catfish.

Tuchel says he chose the four-star, 54-room hotel because it’s “intimate”.

With a grand, pillared reception, a spa, a small suntrap outdoor pool and a downstairs gym, it is an ideal bolthole for the discerning multimillionaire footballer.

A 6oz gilled filet mignon with fingerling potato and green peppercorn sauce will set you back just under £32.



It can be washed down with a bottle of Napa Valley Opus One red wine from the hotel’s well-appointed cellar costing just over £700.

Alan says England will also be supplied with hyperbaric oxygen pods – similar to those Michael Jackson once used.

The FA has asked for a basketball court to be added to the hotel, and they are locating a local swimming pool for the Three Lions to use. The team will have their pick of the city’s golf courses.

The players are unlikely to have the freedom to enjoy the city’s famous jazz clubs.

Or the time to visit the Oz Museum in Wamego – 140 miles west – which boasts a pair of Dorothy’s ruby slippers, a yellow brick road and manikins of the main characters.



At City Hall, I pointed out to Mayor Quinton Lucas that the homicide rate in the KC greater metropolitan area this year – currently 61 – is worryingly high.

The Democrat insists the figures are down around 15 per cent in the city itself on last year and he pledged fans will see a “strong public safety presence no matter where they go”.

Mayor Lucas added: “As for VIPs, they’ll be the safest people in the city and in this country.

“With every base camp announcement that we had – including England – we made sure law enforcement had adequate resources to ensure that they would be very safe throughout.”

As I’m leaving, I asked the mayor the burning question of the summer: “So where is Taylor Swift getting married?”



Laughing, he joked: “I don’t know but I’m sure it will be sold out.”

Some 650,000 visiting fans are expected in KC during the tournament.

Bars will be open for 23 hours a day and the fan zone will encourage supporters to bring their pets dogs.

Organisers hope to capitalise on the success of Bark at the Park occasions at baseball team the Kansas City Royals’ stadium, where fans were allowed to sit in the stands with their canines.

If all goes well, Tuchel’s squad may have to scout out KC tattoo parlours if they’re up for having celebratory inkings.



Whatever happens, the Three Lions will certainly have the feeling that they’re not in Wembley any more.

Sports.title: Middlesbrough threaten legal action if Southampton are not thrown out of play-off final as EFL Commission makes decision
Sports.content:
MIDDLESBROUGH are demanding Southampton be KICKED OUT of the Championship play-off final over Spygate.

The Saints, who beat Middlesbrough over a two-legged semi, have been charged with misconduct with the EFL announcing an Independent Disciplinary Commission will hold a hearing in the next four days.





Fuming Boro have accused finalists Southampton of spying and want the St Mary’s club BOOTED OUT after an intern was allegedly caught filming their training session last week.

But the Independent Disciplinary Commission has denied Boro’s request to participate in the hearing. Meaning, as per standard procedure, the hearing will only involve the EFL and Southampton.

But fuming Boro said in a statement: “Middlesbrough FC notes the decision of the Disciplinary Commission not to permit the club to intervene in the proceedings brought by the EFL against Southampton FC.

“The club regrets that outcome, given we are directly affected by the matters under consideration and hold relevant factual evidence as to the events in question and their competitive impact.

“The conduct at issue, namely the observation and recording of our training session ahead of a fixture of such significance, goes to the heart of sporting integrity and fair competition. In these circumstances, the only appropriate response is a sporting sanction which would prevent Southampton FC from participating in the EFL Championship play-off final.

“We remain hopeful that the EFL, as regulator, will pursue such a sanction before the Disciplinary Commission in order to protect the integrity of the game, safeguard all member clubs, and deter any attempt in the future to obtain an unfair and unlawful advantage in pursuit of promotion to the Premier League. The club reserves all its legal rights.”

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Boro will be allowed to make a written submission, though they will not be able to appeal the commission’s decision, though the EFL and Saints can. However, given the feeling within the walls of the Riverside, Boro would almost certainly still launch a separate compensation claim.

Middlesbrough boss Kim Hellberg and his players remain on red-alert in case they are reinstated, and they will return to training on Monday after being told to hold holiday plans.



Hull City fans are also furious. And they say it is “manifestly unfair” if the Championship play-off final is postponed amid Spygate.

The EFL admitted on Thursday that the £215m Wembley Prem shootout between the Tigers and Southampton may have to be moved from May 23.

Tickets for the scheduled final have now gone on sale to Southampton and Hull supporters, though the EFL said “fans are encouraged to pay particular attention to the terms and conditions”.

But in a further nightmare for league chiefs, any re-arrangement for Wembley would have to take place in the midweek following the current planned date due to other events at the national stadium.

As well as Boro, it has also left Hull, who beat Millwall 2-0 on aggregate, in limbo regarding supporters’ travel plans and their potential opposition.



A Hull City Official Supporters Club statement said: “The Hull City Official Supporters Club are currently liaising with other supporters groups to register our concern over the possible moving of the play-off final with the EFL.

“This is a situation in which we have had no influence but in which we are, both as a football club and supporters, being penalised. Any decision to move the date of the final will result in many of our supporters not only losing out financially but then facing the prospect of being unable to attend the re-arranged fixture.

“Given that this is a situation which has largely resulted from the EFL’s own error in failing to publish the sanctions for a breach of the rule regarding “spying” on opposition teams we feel this is manifestly unfair.”

Hull City sporting director Jared Dublin has stated Sergej Jakirovic and his squad are preparing to take on Saints.

Sun Sport revealed the shock photo of the moment when alleged secret Southampton spy William Salt, an intern analyst, was caught recording Boro train last Thursday ahead of the first leg on Saturday.



Clubs are banned from observing opponents train within 72 hours prior to a game.

Boro have engaged other Championship clubs with at least TWO others understood to believe they were also victims of spying by the South Coast outfit.

The Teessiders’ case is headed up by sports lawyer Nick De Marco. In addition to the picture evidence and CCTV footage, Middlesbrough are also understood to have details of a credit card allegedly used by Salt at the Rockliffe Hall Golf Club, privately owned by club chairman Steve Gibson and next to the training ground.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And they are also understood to have a whistleblower’s statement regarding the alleged act of spying by the Saints from a former Southampton employee.

There is no indication that Southampton boss Tonda Eckert, who walked out of two press conferences after being challenged on the alleged spying, is guilty of any wrongdoing.

Sports.title: Derby County release four players including Wayne Rooney’s cousin and former Premier League star

Former Aston Villa and Bristol City ace Andreas Weimann is also departing after just one season in his second stint at the club.

Rooney, 22, had once looked set for a breakthrough season after impressing during the early part of the 2023-24 campaign.

But the centre-back suffered a serious knee injury during a clash against Bolton Wanderers which ruled him out for the remainder of the season.

Another setback followed before Rooney returned last summer and featured against Burnley in the Carabao Cup.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Sports.title: Man Utd want fellow Wallsend graduate Elliot Anderson to do what Michael Carrick did for Sir Alex Ferguson and win title
Sports.content:
A GEORDIE Wallsend Boys Club talent targeted to bolster the midfield and end Manchester United’s title drought.

That was in 2006. Michael Carrick was one of Sir Alex Ferguson’s most significant signings as United radically reinvented their midfield.



Ferguson masterminded what was, in terms of sheer standards, his greatest title triumph against Jose Mourinho’s Chelsea juggernaut in 2006-07.

Now, 20 years later, Carrick is the United head coach and the club’s dream midfield target. He’s yet another Wallsend product about to start for England at a World Cup.

Elliot Anderson will be on United’s doorstep on Sunday when he plays at Old Trafford for the third time with Nottingham Forest.



The 23-year-old midfielder has performed so superbly this season he is assured of a starting role for Thomas Tuchel in the United States and is wanted by both Manchester clubs.

Sources say Anderson has not made a definitive decision on his future. It is a more delicate matter after the sad death of his mother, Helen, last month.

Multiple agency sources have considered Man City to be favourites and there has been no shift despite the uncertainty over Pep Guardiola’s future.

United have not dropped their interest in Anderson ahead of a summer where competition for central midfielders is expected to be intense among elite clubs.

They have a compelling pitch: join us, play for a fellow Wallsend midfielder and help us win the league. For once, there is more doubt over the City manager than United’s.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

United can ill-afford to miss out on another English midfield maestro three years after Declan Rice and Jude Bellingham slipped the net. United’s English midfield recruit that summer was Mason Mount.

Bellingham visited the United training ground in 2020 and Rice expressed interest in joining the club to Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw during an international break in 2021.

Anderson would command a fee close to £100million but that was the going rate for starting England midfielders Rice and Bellingham in 2023.

Ruben Amorim namechecked Anderson on the eve of United’s reverse fixture with Forest in November, acknowledging he is a “very good player”. Anderson showed how good in front of Amorim at the City Ground.



United fouled Anderson three times that November afternoon. Matheus Cunha was upended four times by United when he ran rings around them for Wolves last season, a performance that convinced them to move for the Brazilian.

Anderson’s switch of play led to Morgan Gibbs-White’s second-half equaliser. Anderson won the majority of his ground duels, played three key passes and ended the afternoon with a 74 per cent passing accuracy.

His average position was slap bang on the halfway line as he managed the desired balance between defence and attack. Anderson is a hybrid of a No6 and a No8, which makes him so appealing to United.

Character is key to recruitment at United these days and, by all accounts, Anderson has remained a modest grafter amid his rise to England regular.



Anderson was watching the television in the gym at Forest’s training complex when his maiden England squad call-up was announced in August.

Team-mates cheered at the news and Anderson stood on a bench and thanked the entire squad: “I couldn’t have done this without you all.”

In 2006, United were still coming to terms with the void in midfield after Roy Keane’s acrimonious departure in November 2005.

The parallels continue in the present: the 34-year-old Casemiro is the same age Keane was when Sir Alex Ferguson tore up his contract.



Casemiro has been vital this season but his importance is overstated. United have not won any of their four Premier League matches without Casemiro in the starting XI and that reflects more unfavourably on his understudy, Manuel Ugarte.

Casemiro and Ugarte are United’s only outright central midfield signings since fellow South American Fred in 2018. It is an area United have neglected for so long that they are prepared to bring in three midfielders this summer alone.

Ferguson did similarly in the mid-2000s. He wanted Owen Hargreaves to join Carrick in 2006 but had to wait a year later, when the Brazilian Anderson also came in.

United were playing catch-up. Between Keane in 1993 and Carrick in 2006, Ferguson signed four midfielders: Juan Sebastian Veron, Eric Djemba-Djemba, Kleberson and Liam Miller. None of them lasted more than two years.



The difference back then was United brought through Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt in the mid-Nineties. They won seven titles in the 13 years between recruiting No16s Keane and Carrick.

Goalscoring is the obvious area for Anderson to improve as he has only four this term, despite Forest also playing 16 games in the Europa League.

Casemiro has tallied nine this term, almost all of them from set pieces. Anderson is Forest’s set-piece taker.

Anderson and Kobbie Mainoo lined up for the first time together in England’s friendly defeat to Japan in March. The duo even stood next to each other for the national anthem.



That would be the dream combination for United as the other midfielders of interest have glaring shortcomings.

Adam Wharton is too slight, Alex Scott has operated at a lower level, Carlos Baleba is solely defensive-minded, so is Aurelien Tchouameni, and Sandro Tonali is more of a deep-lying playmaker. Lower down the food chain, Joao Gomes and Matheus Fernandes could both suffer relegation.

Carrick’s father, Vince, is still involved at Wallsend and Carrick was on the coaching staff at United when they eyed up another Newcastle midfielder in Sean Longstaff seven years ago. Ultimately, the excessive £50m valuation was too off-putting.

Longstaff was still greeted by Carrick at the Old Trafford tunnel when Newcastle played United on Boxing Day in 2019. The first picture of Anderson inside Old Trafford is at practically the same spot, beneath the words ‘Manchester United’.

Carrick is not the only Geordie midfielder who has fared well at the club. Bryan Robson was watching United train at Carrington last week.

Sports.title: Man Utd star Matthijs de Ligt undergoes surgery after one-week injury ruled defender out for SIX MONTHS
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED star Matthijs de Ligt has undergone surgery to address his back injury.

The 26-year-old centre-back is expected to return for United in the early stages of the 2026-27 season.



De Ligt has been sidelined since for six months, having initially been ruled out for week after United beat Crystal Palace on November 30.



But United have announced that the Dutchman has successfully a corrective procedure on his back.

De Ligt timed the announcement with an Instagram post where he told fans he was “disappointed” to miss the upcoming World Cup with the Netherlands.

In a club statement, he said: “Since November I have done everything, pushing myself in every session and exploring every option, to get back to doing what I love, playing football.

“I am grateful to everyone who has supported me throughout a difficult period in my career.

“I remain as determined as ever to represent Manchester United and play in front of our incredible supporters as soon as possible.”

De Ligt had been positive about his rehabilitation while working with club medics over the last six months

The Dutchman had an excellent start to the season, and was voted November player of the season by supporters.

He has not been able to train on grass as United continued to treat his back injury delicately.

United sources said they have not been able to put a timeframe on De Ligt’s return date as it is not a muscular injury.

United are open to bolstering their defence amid the obvious injury concerns around De Ligt and Lisandro Martinez, who has started 11 games this season.

Sports.title: Man Utd star Matthijs de Ligt undergoes surgery and issues emotional statement
Sports.content:
Man Utd star Matthijs de Ligt undergoes surgery and issues emotional statement

Matthijs de Ligt had returned to Manchester United training, in the hope of playing again this season, but his back injury has proved to be more serious than first thought

View 3 Images Matthijs de Ligt has undergone surgery (Image: Poppy Townson - MUFC/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United have confirmed that Matthijs de Ligt has undergone surgery in an attempt to correct a frustrating back injury. De Ligt hasn't played since November because of a back problem and is therefore yet to play under Michael Carrick's management.

‌



He returned to United training last month and had originally hoped to play again this season. But, together with the club, it was decided that going under the knife would be beneficial for the 26-year-old Netherlands international, who will miss the World Cup.

‌



Sharing a photo of himself in a hospital bed, De Ligt wrote on Instagram: "After 6 months of treatment and working hard to get back, surgery was the only option left. I’m disappointed I couldn’t help the team the last 6 months and obviously missing out on the World Cup but I am looking forward to doing everything to get back in front of the fans and feeling better again."

‌



His Netherlands team-mates Frenkie de Jong and Micky van de Ven were among those to send supportive messages, as well as ex-United midfielder Christian Eriksen.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Michael Carrick gives telling response to Man Utd job question after latest update READ MORE :

Sir Jim Ratcliffe makes final Michael Carrick decision as Man Utd prepare five offers READ MORE :

United said: "Matthijs de Ligt has undergone successful surgery to address a back injury. Having diligently worked throughout his rehabilitation process, the decision was made that a corrective procedure was the best course of action."

‌



De Ligt told the club website: “Since November I have done everything, pushing myself in every session and exploring every option, to get back to doing what I love, playing football.

“I am grateful to everyone who has supported me throughout a difficult period in my career. I remain as determined as ever to represent Manchester United and play in front of our incredible supporters as soon as possible.”

3 View 3 Images Matthijs de Ligt has undergone surgery (Image: mdeligt_/Instagram) 3 View 3 Images He's been out since November (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



De Ligt made 14 appearances for United this season before being sidelined in November. He has since missed 24 matches due to the back problem. "It's difficult to say, just because it's taken that much time," Carrick said in late March about De Ligt's return timeline.

"With backs sometimes you think it's all right and all of a sudden it's not quite right. We're just being patient and working through it. We'll give him time and try to get him back as quickly as we can, but it's really difficult to say."

On the prospect of De Ligt getting surgery, Carrick added: "I don't want to get into that at this stage. We'll try and do whatever we can to help and we're working through that now. I'm not trying to hide anything. He's improving. It's just not as quick as we all hope."

Sports.title: Middlesbrough demand Southampton are kicked OUT of play-offs in new Spygate statement
Sports.content:
Middlesbrough demand Southampton are kicked OUT of play-offs in new Spygate statement

Middlesbrough have maintained that Southampton have to be kicked out of the play-off final to maintain sporting integrity following the Spygate scandal that marred their semi-final

View 2 Images Middlesbrough still hope to see Southampton kicked out of the play-off final (Image: Warren Little/Getty Images)

Middlesbrough have said they "regret" that the EFL will not let the club be part of any legal proceedings against Southampton given they are "directly affected by the matters" - and hope to see them kicked out of the play-off final.

‌



The Teesside club were beaten by the Saints in the play-off semi-final following the Spygate saga, but maintain hope that the authorities will issue a "sporting sanction" - which could see Middlesbrough go through to the final at Southampton's expense.

‌



The Saints were charged by the EFL before the first-leg at the Riverside Stadium as a staff member was caught watching their opponents train. The first game finished goalless before Southampton claimed a 2-1 victory on their own patch.

‌



That earned them the right to face Hull at Wembley later this month, but the EFL are investigating with the matter from the closed as Middlesbrough ramp up the pressure to "to protect the integrity of the game".

They said in a statement: "Middlesbrough FC notes the decision of the Disciplinary Commission not to permit the club to intervene in the proceedings brought by the EFL against Southampton FC.

Date Championship play-off final could be played as Spygate row causes chaos READ MORE :

"The club regrets that outcome, given we are directly affected by the matters under consideration and hold relevant factual evidence as to the events in question and their competitive impact.

‌



"The conduct at issue, namely the observation and recording of our training session ahead of a fixture of such significance, goes to the heart of sporting integrity and fair competition. In these circumstances, the only appropriate response is a sporting sanction which would prevent Southampton FC from participating in the EFL Championship play-off final.

"We remain hopeful that the EFL, as regulator, will pursue such a sanction before the Disciplinary Commission in order to protect the integrity of the game, safeguard all member clubs, and deter any attempt in the future to obtain an unfair and unlawful advantage in pursuit of promotion to the Premier League. The club reserves all its legal rights."

View 2 Images Middlesbrough boss Kim Hellberg cut an emotional figure after full-time (Image: Warren Little, Getty Images)

Article continues below

Boro boss Kim Hellberg cut an emotional figure after the loss earlier in the week and said: "It breaks my heart in terms of all those things I believe in. That's the thing. I don't care if there are other rules in different countries. This is England where football is the biggest thing. That's my feelings about it. I think it's disgraceful. It makes me very sad."

Southampton have remained coy and boss Tonda Eckert walked out of a press conference at the weekend as he fielded questions on the scandal - and then repeated the trick in the aftermath of the Saints' win on Tuesday when he was asked if he was a cheat.

Sports.title: Tottenham to face new spending rule if they go down as Championship clubs 'vote for change'
Sports.content:
Tottenham to face new spending rule if they go down as Championship clubs 'vote for change'

Championship clubs have voted on a proposal to align with the Premier League from next season by replacing their profitability and sustainability rules

View 2 Images Tottenham Hotspur could face new spending rules (Image: Rob Newell - CameraSport via Getty Images)

Tottenham Hotspur will have to contend with a new spending rule if they are relegated from the Premier League to the Sky Bet Championship. Clubs in the second-tier have today voted through major changes to the league's financial regulations, following support from 20 of the division’s 24 teams.

‌



Clubs have backed plans to replace the current profitability and sustainability (P&S) system with a squad cost ratio model (SCR) from next season. The new rules will align the division more closely with the Premier League's new rules and cap spending on football costs at 85 per cent of total revenue.

‌



SCR expenses are directly tied to the first team, which includes player wages, manager salaries, agent fees, and the yearly amortisation of player transfer fees. They are consolidated into a single budget pool that represents the true cost of the squad.

‌



If clubs in the Championship don’t comply with the rules, then a non-negotiable sporting penalty is applied in the season that an offence occurs. Exceeding limits incurs an automatic six-point deduction.

The point deduction increases based on the size of the breach. For every £6.5 million spent beyond the ceiling, an additional one-point penalty is added.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Spurs return to Premier League action next week with their Premier League future still uncertain. They are currently two points clear of the drop zone, having secured just 38 points from 36 games so far this season, taking until April 25 to win a league game in 2026.

Monday's 1-1 draw with Leeds United saw Tottenham miss the chance to pull even further clear of West Ham United at the bottom of the table. The Hammers were beaten 1-0 by Arsenal on Sunday and, at one stage during the Spurs vs Leeds game, were five points adrift with two matches remaining.

But that gap is now two, with the Hammers facing Newcastle United on Sunday afternoon before Spurs return to action against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge on Tuesday night. Asked what is overarching emotion was at seeing his old club battle to avoid the drop, former Spurs chairman Daniel Levy admitted on Thursday: "Emptiness…I'm feeling the pain but I'm optimistic that we'll get through it.

‌



"It's been very, very difficult - Spurs is in my blood. I could never have envisioned this at the beginning of the season. Obviously incredibly disappointed. Let's look forward and very much hope that next season we're still in the Premier League."

View 2 Images Roberto De Zerbi's Spurs are still in a Premier League relegation battle (Image: (Maynard Manyowa/News Images/NurPhoto via Getty Images))

He added: “I’m optimistic that we will remain in the Premier League. I think Tottenham has a great coach, and all the fans and all the employees and everyone now are behind this coach.

‌



“Let’s hope that the players can do it for the last two games. Like every fan there’d be emptiness in the stomach. But, we will bounce back.

“Let’s be optimistic and hope that doesn’t happen. I just hope at this moment in time that Tottenham manages to remain in the Premier League.”

Sports.title: Pep Guardiola makes startling admission on Man City schedule before FA Cup final
Sports.content:
Pep Guardiola makes startling admission on Man City schedule before FA Cup final

Manchester City are ending the season with four games in 12 days and Pep Guardiola has been given a tough task for Saturday's FA Cup final, with the Premier League title race still on

View 2 Images Pep Guardiola was honest about Manchester City's preparations (Image: Hayters TV)

Pep Guardiola says that Manchester City have not been able to train before the FA Cup final against Chelsea due to their tight schedule. City travel to Wembley on Saturday for the chance of winning a second domestic trophy this season in between Premier League matches.

‌



Guardiola's side beat Crystal Palace 3-0 on Wednesday night to keep the pressure on league-leaders Arsenal. It was the first of four games in 12 days, with the Palace match rearranged from earlier in the season due to City's run in the Carabao Cup.

‌



City are heavy favourites to add the Carabao Cup they won against Arsenal at Wembley in late March when they take on Calum McFarlane's out-of-form Chelsea side. They will then travel down to play Bournemouth on Tuesday before finishing the season at home to Aston Villa next Sunday.

‌



They are two points behind Arsenal, who are in pole position ahead of games against Burnley and Palace, but Guardiola still has a task on his hands to juggle priorities. Asked if the Bournemouth game would influence his selection for Saturday, Guardiola responded immediately: "Zero. It's the final of the FA Cup."

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

Arsenal discover huge VAR error in title race as Premier League panel confirm mistakes READ MORE :

Date Championship play-off final could be played as Spygate row causes chaos READ MORE :

"I would prefer seven days like Chelsea had, but when you win the Carabao Cup and reach the final of one of these domestic trophies you have to live with less days," he added in a pre-match press conference on Friday.

‌



"It happened in the past when [we won] titles and it's not necessary to remember. It's the schedule. It's what it is. Of course, it's not ideal, it is what it is, we did it in the past and we'll have to do it tomorrow. The big clubs, you find, when you are in the more difficult circumstances than the opponents you do extra, you try to do it and this is what you have to do. It's simple.

"It's not the perfect scenario to prepare for the final because we did not train absolutely anything since the last game against Crystal Palace but I rely a lot on what we have to do - and we're going to try."

View 2 Images Manchester City are in their fourth successive FA Cup final, but have lost the last two (Image: Getty)

‌



Asked if he had reviewed the 1-1 draw with Chelsea on January 4, Guardiola said: "I didn't have time. I will do it on the train down (tomorrow). They played different in each half: first half more passive, second half more aggressive, we had our momentum and at the end they equalise.

"We have to read what they are going to do. I saw their last game against Liverpool, because I like to see what the vibe and the tone of the team is like. They suffered the first 15 or 20 minutes, but Anfield always happens, and afterwards they came back with a goal from Enzo Fernandez and the time was good."

Although they have a busy schedule, City do have the advantage of a near fully-fit squad, with Rodri the only injury doubt. Erling Haaland and Nico O'Reilly were among those to be rested for the comfortable win over Palace and should be fresh for Wembley.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick gives telling response to Man Utd job question after latest update
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick gives telling response to Man Utd job question after latest update

Michael Carrick is expected to be confirmed as Manchester United's next permanent head coach before the end of the season after impressing in an interim capacity

View 2 Images Michael Carrick is poised to land the Manchester United job full-time (Image: Offside via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick refused to be drawn on speculation that he is poised to be offered the Manchester United job on a permanent basis but did admit he expects his future to be decided 'pretty soon'.

‌



The former United midfielder has impressed since succeeding Ruben Amorim on an interim basis back in January, winning 10 of his 15 games at the helm. That run of form has lifted the Red Devils from seventh to third in the Premier League standings, with United already assured of a return to the Champions League next year.

‌



Suggestions that the 44-year-old would be entrusted with the role on a full-time basis have intensified since United clinched qualification for the Champions League. Reports emerged earlier this week outlining that Carrick was to be recommended to Sir Jim Ratcliffe as the preferred candidate in the search for a new permanent head coach.

‌



And while Carrick was questioned over his future ahead of Manchester United's game against Nottingham Forest this weekend, the former Middlesbrough chief was giving little away.

Sir Jim Ratcliffe makes final Michael Carrick decision as Man Utd prepare five offers READ MORE :

Jamie Carragher backs down over Casemiro jibe after Man Utd star hits back READ MORE :

“There’s two games to go, apart from that there’s not much else to say,” he said during his press conference on Friday. “The situation is pretty clear for us all. Same as in preparing for the game.

“It’s a unique football club, a special club. Immensely proud to have come back and been a part of it, as a supporter and ex-player, as a pure supporter to be in a position to come back and help and move forward was important. To make a big step, and back in the Champions League is good, we’re happy with the work we’ve done so far.

‌



“The future for me is going to be decided pretty soon, we knew that. Nothing has changed, there is no big swing on that.”

View 2 Images Carrick has turned United's season around (Image: Catherine Ivill - AMA, Getty Images)

United play their final home game of the season on Sunday when they host Nottingham Forest at Old Trafford. While it remains to be seen if Carrick's future will be wrapped up by then, he confirmed he will address supporters on the pitch post-match.

‌



“I think that’s important regardless of the situation. The supporters are a massive part of this club. We thank them - and I certainly thank them - for the season and the support, the last four months for me personally,” he said.

“Regardless of that [his future], for what we’ve gone through and that connection, the players have felt that, it’s important we have that anyway.

“It’s important for me to thank the fans for that.”

Sports.title: Liverpool can land top Premier League defender for free despite rival's 'agreement'
Sports.content:
Liverpool can land top Premier League defender for free despite rival's 'agreement'

Liverpool are in the market for a new centre-back this summer but face competition for Bournemouth's Marcos Senesi, who has already reportedly agreed personal terms with Tottenham

View 2 Images Marcos Senesi is leaving Bournemouth this summer (Image: Robin Jones/Getty Images)

Liverpool will have to move fast if they want to sign Marcos Senesi as a free agent upon his departure from Bournemouth. The Cherries confirmed on Friday that the centre-back will leave when his contract expires this summer - and there is bound to be a lot of interest in the Argentina international.

‌



Senesi has been one of the stand-out performers for Andoni Iraola's side this season, making 37 appearances across all competitions. He has helped Bournemouth reach sixth place in the Premier League, with a good chance of securing European football next season with two games to go.

‌



But the 29-year-old has rejected multiple offers of a new deal with Bournemouth and will be leaving the club this summer, like Iraola. Liverpool are among the clubs who have been linked with Senesi, yet Tottenham have reportedly stolen a march on their rivals.

‌



According to talkSPORT, Senesi has agreed personal terms with Spurs and is in line to move to north London, if they avoid relegation. Tottenham are unbeaten in their last four games and sit two points above West Ham in the final relegation place ahead of the weekend's penultimate round of fixtures.

Liverpool are in the market for a centre-back this summer, with uncertainty surrounding Joe Gomez's future and with Ibrahima Konate yet to sign a new contract. Captain Virgil van Dijk is now 34 years old and, with Giovanni Leoni having suffered a season-ending knee injury soon after arriving last summer, there is still a need for new players, despite the pending £60million arrival of Jeremy Jacquet from Rennes.

‌



Senesi has been the bedrock behind Bournemouth's climb up the table in 2026, partnering James Hill to 11 clean sheets during their current 16-game unbeaten run. Having arrived from Feyenoord in 2022, he has 124 appearances for the club in total.

View 2 Images Bournemouth's Marcos Senesi could join Liverpool as a free agent (Image: Robin Jones - AFC Bournemouth/AFC Bournemouth via Getty Images)

Promoter Queensberry confirmed: "Fabio Wardley has activated the rematch clause following his defeat in last week's WBO world title fight against Daniel Dubois at the Co-op Live in Manchester.

"All parties will now work towards a rematch of their fight of the year contender for later in 2026."

Wardley did not require hospital treatment at the weekend and is recovering from the facial injuries he suffered in the bout.

Sports.title: Ireland's all-action McKenna returns on June 6, live on Sky Sports
Sports.content:
Stevie McKenna has signed a long-term deal with Zuffa Boxing and will return to action on June 6, live on Sky Sports.

On the Zuffa Boxing 07 bill at the Bournemouth International Centre, headlined by Chris Billam-Smith vs Ryan Rozicki, McKenna will fight American veteran Casey James Streeter.

Irish contender McKenna is always exciting to watch. He delivered thrilling fights in the UK in 2024. A three-round war with Joe Laws saw McKenna hit the canvas but ultimately prevail as he dropped Laws four times in all.

In another tremendous clash, he was edged out by Lee Cutler on a majority decision over 10 rounds in their fight in Liverpool.

Rivals McKenna and Cutler will both fight in separate bouts on the June 6 bill in the latter's Bournemouth hometown.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch new angles of the incredible fight between Joe Laws and Stevie McKenna that had five knockdowns in just three rounds

His loss to Cutler in that all-action classic is the sole defeat McKenna has suffered in his professional career.

McKenna was an amateur standout, winning gold medals at the Haringey Box Cup and Commonwealth Youth Games before turning pro in 2019.

Before he met Cutler he went on a 15 bout winning streak, taking 14 of those victories inside the distance.

He has registered 11 of those knockouts in three rounds or less.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the whole first round between Stephen McKenna and Joe Laws as both fighters suffered knockdowns in the opening three minutes

Streeter, his opponent on June 6, has a 15-3-2 (6) record. From Portland, Maine Streeter makes his UK debut following a stoppage defeat to Leo Ruiz on Zuffa Boxing 03.

Zuffa Boxing 07 will be broadcast live on Sky Sports in the UK and Ireland. As well as the battle between Bournemouth's hometown hero Billam-Smith and Canadian KO artist Rozicki, an all-British chief support pits long-time cruiserweight contenders Jack Massey and Cheavon Clarke against one another.

Tickets are on sale now and can be purchased via BIC.co.uk.

Host Kate Tracey…
